title: BuiltModel v2
description: The one model format the viewer reads (app/docs/DESIGN.md section 5). It is the format of bank_test/src/bank_model.json and hotel_test/src/hotel_model.json, which are valid v1 byte for byte; the suite and the house are converted to it by the seed. Plan coordinates are metres in the model frame (drawing coordinates minus `offset`); three.js maps plan (x, y) to (x, z = -y). Heights z0 / z1 are metres above the level of the part's floor. The format carries no version field: the version lives in the version sidecar (version.json: modelFormat 'built-model/1' or 'built-model/2'). v2 (the rooms milestone, app/docs/rooms/DESIGN.md R-12.1) only adds optional things, and no v1 field changes meaning, so every v1 model is a valid v2 model: the part kinds tread, landing and ceiling, the part fit 'storey' and the part's `stair`, the top-level `stairways` and `spaces`, and `rooms[].space`. A model is v2 when it has the `stairways` key (an empty list when no stair climbs): that key switches the viewer's foot-based walker on. Cross-references (floor keys, furniture kinds, supports, approach ids) are checked by the parsers (parseBuiltModel in the viewer, hand-written TypeScript with no validator library at run time; walkthrough_api.builtmodel in the API), not by this schema: DESIGN.md 5.6. The schema compiles with ajv 8 in strict mode (Ajv2020) and with Python jsonschema (Draft 2020-12).

projectNo.description: The office's project number, if any.

source.description: Names of the drawings or pictures the model was built from (display only).

offset.description: Drawing coordinates = model coordinates + offset (plan metres), on the shared grid the floors are lined up on; a floor drawn elsewhere on its sheet adds floors[].sheetShift. Used by the furniture CSV and the 3ds Max script.

photoName.description: Names photos (<photoName>_<Mode>_..png), the furniture CSV (<photoName>_furniture_list.csv) and the local storage key.

maxPrefix.description: Prefix of the 3ds Max layer and object names.

floors.description: In level order, lowest first; keys unique.

pictureFrame.description: Floors read from a picture: where the picture lies under the model ('Plan picture' tick).

furnitureKinds.description: Only the kinds that occur, in the kinds table's order (furniture/README.md).

stairways.description: v2 (optional): the stairs that can be climbed in Walk. Present in every model built with the new rule (empty when no stair climbs): its presence marks a v2 model. Ids unique.

spaces.description: v2 (optional): the rooms with their outlines, named or not. `rooms` stays what it is in v1: the drawn names, one label each. Ids unique.

floorKey.description: Letters, digits and underscore only: replay captions name floors as {<key>level} / {<key>height}.

ring.description: A closed outline, plan metres; the last point is not repeated (a repeated last point is tolerated).

perFloor.description: Keyed by floor key; a floor without an entry has none (empty).

level.description: Floor level (m) above the project datum; the slab's top.

wallHeight.description: Height of the walls of this floor (m above its level).

stack.description: v1 extension (optional). Floors of one stack are walked as one building (Walk shows the whole stack, PgUp/PgDn move within it). Default 'main'.

sheetShift.description: v1 extension (optional, default [0, 0]). Where this floor's plan sits on its source sheet, relative to the shared grid the model uses: sheet coordinates = model coordinates + offset + sheetShift (plan metres). The house's upper floor: [74.021, 0] (its plan is drawn beside the ground plan on one sheet). Provenance only: the viewer, the CSV and the Max script do not read it (they use the shared grid).

partKind.description: bank/hotel kinds: wall column lintel sill parapet glass mullion railing single step slab; v1 extensions for the converted models: pane (house window panes), balustrade low builtin deck post (presidential suite); v2: tread and landing (a climbable stair's step and landing solids: walked on, never colliders; each names its stairway in `stair`) and ceiling (a ceiling plate, shown in Walk and Ghost only). How each kind is drawn: DESIGN.md 5.4, rooms/DESIGN.md R-9.

z0.description: Bottom, m above the floor level.

z1.description: Top, m above the floor level; z1 > z0.

follow.description: Its top follows the wall height: when Build settings change the floor's wall height H0 -> H the part scales by H / H0 about the floor level (unless `fit` says otherwise).

label.description: What the builder called it (an opening id, a Revit type name, 'mullion', ...).

fit.description: v1 extension (optional): how the part answers a wall-height change instead of scaling. 'top': z0 stays and z1 becomes the new wall top (the part vanishes when the wall is no higher than z0): the house's lintels and the panes that reach the wall top. 'clip': z0 and z1 stay, cut off at the new wall top: the house's sills and other panes. v2 'storey': the part scales with its stairway's storey (the level difference of the stairway's `from` and `to` floors) when Build settings change a level: treads, landings and the wall pieces cut under a stair, which name their stairway in `stair`.

stair.description: v2 (optional): the id of the stairway the part belongs to (treads, landings, wall pieces cut under a stair). The part lies on that stairway's `from` floor. Every tread and landing has one.

plinth.description: v1 extension (optional, slabs only): the slab stands on the ground (z0 = -level): when Build settings change the floor's level it stretches so its foot stays at y = 0 (the house's ground plate).

below.description: Tread lines below the cut: drawn as thin strips lying on the floor.

above.description: Flights above the cut (the next storey's): faint lines.

panels.description: v1 extension (optional): tread lines drawn as 0.15 m high upright panels standing on the floor (the house's stairs).

flatSegments.description: x1, y1, x2, y2, ... plan metres; length a multiple of 4 (checked by the parsers).

voidMark.description: A hole in the floor plate (stair, lift shaft ...), for tests and the Max script; the hole itself is in the slab part.

closure.description: A wall gap closed because an object stands in it (the bank's ATM).

label.description: Shown over the model (as text, never as HTML).

area.description: m2; bigger rooms keep their label's spot when labels would overlap.

space.description: v2 (optional): the id of the space (room) this drawn name belongs to, on the same floor; absent when it belongs to none.

id.description: Unique in the model ('S1'); parts name it in `stair`.

from.description: The lower floor: the stair's treads and landings are parts of this floor.

to.description: A higher floor of the same stack, usually the next.

kind.description: 'straight', 'L', 'U' or another word for its shape (display and tests).

riser.description: Riser height (m): the level difference of `to` and `from` divided by `risers`.

width.description: The median riser length of the narrowest flight (m).

bottom.description: The first point of `walk`, on the lower floor.

top.description: The last point of `walk`, on the upper floor.

walk.description: The walking line, bottom to top: from 1.0 m before the first riser, through the middle of each flight and landing, to 1.0 m past the last riser (model frame).

direction.description: How the bottom end was found: 'word', 'arrow', 'cut', 'floors', 'staff' ...

stairway.description: v2: a stair that can be climbed in Walk (rooms/DESIGN.md R-8.5). Read by the viewer's climbing switch, the stair probe and the replay's facts. Builders may add evidence fields: extra properties are allowed.

id.description: Unique in the model; rooms[].space names it.

name.description: The room's own name; '' when it has none. Drawing or staff text: shown as text only.

names.description: Every drawn name in the room.

source.description: What closed it: the wall network, a drawn room outline, or a staff fix.

ceiling.description: false when staff marked the room 'no ceiling'.

space.description: v2: one room (rooms/DESIGN.md R-3.4): a face of the wall network of at least 1 m2 whose edge is at least half structure. Read by nothing in the viewer in this milestone.

id.description: Unique in the model; furniture 'approach' lists name these.

exterior.description: Only one side has floor: walked from inside only.

lintel.description: What stands above the head; null or absent: nothing (passages, windows to the top).

opening.description: Doors, windows and passages: what was cut is already in `parts`; these records drive tests, the furniture approach rule and the Max script. Builders add their own evidence fields (glazed, jambs, leaves, a, b, floorSide ...): extra properties are allowed.

inside.description: The sides to walk at the glass from.

probe.description: A spot on glass that Walk must not pass (tests).

glass.description: Hidden with the Glass tick (it wraps glass).

skin.description: An invisible Walk collider around a piece thinner than Walk's ray spacing.

file.description: The picture as the builder saw it (relative to the model file); the store maps it to an asset (version.json assets[].modelRef).

height.description: mm, the office default the height box starts with.

base.description: mm, the underside above the floor.

blocks.description: Walk stops you at it (the 'stops' tick's default).

count.description: The number of pieces of this kind (the API refuses a mismatch; the viewer warns and counts the pieces).

on.description: The id of the piece it stands on (its underside is that piece's top), else null.

approach.description: Ids of the openings (doors, passages) this piece stands in front of; while 'Keep doorways clear' is ticked such a piece does not stop Walk.
